Column names for TextGrid landmark tiers

Source: R/landmarks.R
landmark_prefixes.Rd

The column prefix p that attach_landmarks() uses for each tier, whose columns are then p, p_start, p_end and p_i. A tier gets the same prefix whichever tiers are attached with it, and in whatever order, as long as all_tiers is the same.

Usage

landmark_prefixes(
  tier_names,
  all_tiers = tier_names,
  reserved = c("token", "time", "f0", "intensity", "f0_corrected", "f0_original",
    "edited", "token_dropped", "n_missing", "has_gap", "point", "time_prop",
    "voiced_run")
)

Arguments

tier_names

Tier names to give prefixes.

all_tiers

Every tier name the columns could come from, such as all interval tiers of the corpus from tg_interval_tiers(). The numbering depends only on this set, so pass the same one in every call. Names in tier_names but not in all_tiers are numbered after it.

reserved

Column names a tier must not take. Defaults to the columns that F0 Extraction, F0 Correction and the Start page write into the f0 data, voiced_run included.

Value

A character vector of prefixes, named by tier_names.

Details

The prefix keeps the letters, in any script, and the digits of the tier name. ASCII letters are lowercased. Any other run of characters becomes _, and _ at either end is dropped; a name with nothing left becomes "tier". So "Syllable (broad)" gives syllable_broad, and a tier named in Chinese characters or IPA keeps its name. Names are first put in Unicode NFC form (when the utf8 package is installed) and combining marks are then dropped, so in a UTF-8 locale every prefix is a syntactic R name unless it starts with a digit.

A prefix already in use gets _2, _3 and so on: when two tiers give the same prefix, or when a prefix or one of its columns is in reserved. A tier whose name is already its own prefix keeps it, and the others are numbered in the byte order of their names. So tiers syllable, Syllable and syllable! give syllable, syllable_2 and syllable_3, and a tier named time gives time_2. Columns made later from a prefix (p_t01, p_tseq, p_tbound, p_f0_dur) are kept apart too.

Examples

landmark_prefixes(c("syllable", "Syllable (broad)", "time"))
#>         syllable Syllable (broad)             time 
#>       "syllable" "syllable_broad"         "time_2" 
# The same prefix whichever of the tiers is attached
tiers <- c("syllable", "Syllable", "syllable!")
landmark_prefixes("Syllable", all_tiers = tiers)
#>     Syllable 
#> "syllable_2" 
landmark_prefixes(tiers)
#>     syllable     Syllable    syllable! 
#>   "syllable" "syllable_2" "syllable_3" 
# A tier named in Chinese characters keeps its name
landmark_prefixes(intToUtf8(c(0x58F0, 0x8C03)))
#>   声调 
#> "声调"
